title: Did Marijuana Prohibition Cost Trump the Election Once and the Democrats Twice?

content_html_sanitized:
The latest news is that President Trump will make a decision on whether to reschedule marijuana in a few weeks.

 

As usual, the reporting has been incompetent and described the move as meaning that marijuana is “less dangerous.”

See Trump considers reclassifying marijuana as less dangerous drug: report

 

Most importantly, it would drop the absurd claim that marijuana has no medical value. That would make it much easier for veterans to be able to get it.

 

Roughly 90% of Americans are in favor of legalizing medical marijuana.

 

I try to keep MarijuanaNews on topic and out of partisan politics for obvious reasons. As a libertarian that is fairly easy. To quote The Kingston Trio, I don’t like anyone very much.

 

For a long time, the marijuana issue was largely blacked out of the public discourse, but by 2016 support was over 50%

 

Then in 2000, Bill Clinton actually came out for decriminalization, sixteen years before his wife ran for President against Trump and lost.

See Clinton Says Marijuana Should Be Decriminalized. Now He Tells Us!

 

When Trump upset Clinton, support for medical marijuana was up to 93%, but then he appointed Jefferson Beauregard Sessionsas his Attorney General, and even let Sessions, a rabid Prohibitionist, attempt to block state medical marijuana laws.

See What Jeff Sessions doesn’t understand about medical marijuana

 

Then four years later, Trump lost to Joe Biden, a lifelong Prohibitionist who had at least moderated on medical marijuana.

See Did Marijuana Prohibition Cost Trump the Election?

 

And Biden Sort of Decides On Marijuana Legalization: He Is Sort of Still Against It

 

Four years later, the Biden Administration was still struggling over the process of taking marijuana out of Schedule 1 with heroin and admitting that it has medical value.

See Marijuana Is In Schedule One. Fentanyl Is In Schedule 2. Think About It.

 

When Biden finally stepped down and let Harris run she came out for legalization just over thirty days before the election.

 

However, when Joe Rogan, the enormously popular podcaster, who supports marijuana legalization, invited her to appear on his show, she made clear that she didn’t want to talk about marijuana policy and declined the invitation.

See Kamala Harris ‘Didn’t Want To Talk About Marijuana Legalization’ With Joe Rogan, Podcaster Says Of Interview That Never Happened

 

Rogan then endorsed Trump and the Harris camp could not figure out how they lost.
